name: Test Driven Development Conventions
description: This module defines the naming, formatting, and structural style conventions to follow whenever writing, implementing, or reviewing test driven development code or output, so results stay consistent with the existing test driven development style guide.
content:
This module defines the naming, formatting, and structural style conventions to follow whenever writing, implementing, or reviewing test driven development code or output, so results stay consistent with the existing test driven development style guide.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Keep test driven development outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
2. Measure before optimizing any test driven development bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
3. Check that test driven development terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
4. Prefer the simplest test driven development approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
5. Surface known limitations of a chosen test driven development approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
6. When test driven development decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
7. Re-check edge cases relevant to test driven development (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
8. Prefer explicit, readable test driven development solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
9. When multiple test driven development strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
10. Validate test driven development outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid introducing new test driven development abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not skip documenting test driven development assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid mixing unrelated test driven development concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not apply generic test driven development advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for test driven development, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
